title: Patchlook — Open-source Git diff viewer for macOS, Windows & Linux
description: A native, open-source Git viewer for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Review local changes and Linux repositories over SSH. Read-only by default, with optional selective staging.
intro: Patchlook is a free, open-source Git diff viewer for local repositories and Linux servers. Review changes, explore history, and stage just what you need.
screenshot_alt: Patchlook displaying its own Git history and an inline diff, in light and dark themes.
review_body: Read diffs side by side or inline. Fold away unchanged lines, compare images, and find a commit by its message or SHA.
stage_body: Unlock read/write mode to stage files or change blocks. Undo staging and discard operations within the current repository session. Commit with your usual tools.
ssh_body: Connect over SSH to browse a Linux repository without cloning it. Remote browsing stays read-only. Passwords and passphrases are never saved.
get_description: Free and open source. Pick your platform and open a repository.
windows_detail: Unzip and run. No installer needed.
linux_detail: Built on Ubuntu 24.04. X11 or Wayland.
built_with: Built with Rust and GPUI Kit.
brew_copy_error: Select the command and copy it manually.
faq_intro: Free and open source under the MIT license.
faq_platforms_answer: {mac_requirements}; {windows_requirements}; {linux_requirements}. {linux_detail} Linux also needs Vulkan and compatible system libraries. Local repositories require Git; SSH connections require OpenSSH.
faq_staging_question: Can Patchlook change files or create commits?
faq_staging_answer: Patchlook starts read-only. Unlock read/write mode for local repositories to stage or unstage files and change blocks, or discard an unwanted block. Staging and discard operations can be undone in the current repository session. Commit, checkout, and push remain in your usual Git tools.
faq_ssh_question: Can I browse a remote repository without cloning it?
faq_ssh_answer: Yes. Patchlook connects to Linux servers over SSH using a password, private key, or SSH agent. The server needs Git, but not Patchlook. Remote browsing is always read-only. Passwords and key passphrases are not saved.
